hero.headline: Your AI sculpts your game assets.
hero.lede: Glina turns a text prompt into a verified, game-ready GLB. A Brama-routed model writes Blender Python and runs it in a live Blender MCP session. A structural gate passes or fails the result before it counts as done.
hero.metaDescription: Glina turns a text prompt into a verified, game-ready GLB through Brama and a live Blender MCP session, behind a structural quality gate that fails, never warns.

sections.heading: Raw text-to-3D output ships unverified.
sections.lede: A game project needs hundreds of modeled, budgeted GLB assets. Hand-modeling them is slow, and raw AI output arrives broken.

items.title: Broken meshes
items.text: AI-generated geometry arrives with no mesh or primitive sanity check, so defects reach the game.

items.title: Blown triangle budgets
items.text: Nothing enforces a budget. Glina's gate checks a default of 6000 triangles, plus or minus 100 percent.

items.title: Missing materials
items.text: Materials, skins, and animation presence go unchecked unless a gate verifies them before the asset counts as done.

sections.heading: From prompt to verified GLB.
sections.lede: Every generation follows the same path: prompt, model, Blender, gate.

items.title: Write a text prompt
items.text: Describe the prop, weapon, or character you need as plain text.

items.title: Brama routes the model
items.text: Model access goes only through Brama, the Wisent model router. There is no direct provider API code in the package.

items.title: The model writes Blender Python
items.text: The Brama-routed model writes bpy code for the asset.

items.title: Blender MCP executes it
items.text: The code runs in a live Blender session through a Blender MCP server, uvx blender-mcp by default. Never hand-rolled sockets.

items.title: The gate decides
items.text: The gate checks a valid glTF container, mesh sanity, the triangle budget, materials, file size, and an optional render smoke. It fails the job and never warns.

sections.heading: Hard rules, never bypassed.
sections.lede: The control questions developers ask, answered by the package itself.

items.question: Where do my secrets live?
items.answer: Only in Skarbiec. Config holds skarbiec://<item>/<field> references, and the loader rejects inline secrets and credential-shaped environment variables.

items.question: How does model access work?
items.answer: Only through Brama, the Wisent model router. Direct provider API paths were deleted at the owner's demand, not gated.

items.question: How is Blender controlled?
items.answer: Only through a Blender MCP server, uvx blender-mcp by default. Never hand-rolled sockets.

items.question: What drives the browser layer?
items.answer: Only the Weles MCP stdio server, weles-mcp. Never a local Chromium profile.

sections.heading: Install the CLI and sculpt your first asset.
sections.lede: One npm install ships two bins: glina for the command line and glina-mcp as an MCP stdio server for agent hosts. Glina started as the asset pipeline of the browser RTS simple-rts-unity and now ships as a standalone Wisent product with a CLI and a macOS desktop app.
